report.releaseDate: 10 Nov 2026 (FY26 trading update, 1 Jul–31 Oct); financial base: H1 2026 results, 10 Sep 2026
report.currency: EUR (tables in €m; ~USD at EUR/USD 1.1214, ECB fix 10 Nov 2026)
report.verdict: Playtech's third guidance upgrade of 2026 lifts FY26 adj. EBITDA to ">€300m" (~$336m) — +52% on FY25 and 7.5% above the €279m consensus — on the back of a Hard Rock Digital/PMR windfall in Florida that management itself says is already being competed away. The quality of 2026 is unarguable (H1 FCF €101.0m, net cash, 10% of shares retired in a year), but the same RNS effectively pre-announces a down year: FY27 consensus of €266m sits 11% below the FY26 floor, with PMR wallet-share loss, a Brazilian market shutdown and a full year of 40% UK RGD all landing at once. The shares' intraday +4.5% fading to −1.0% at the close is the right read: peak-year earnings, not a re-rating.

kpis.delta: −11% vs FY26 floor; mgmt flags headwinds

summary: **Scope note — FY26 actuals are not yet published.** Playtech reports half-yearly; the FY26 results are due ~March 2027. This note is built on the 10 Nov 2026 trading update (covering 1 Jul–31 Oct 2026, which contains guidance only, no P&L figures) layered on the reviewed H1 2026 results (10 Sep 2026). H2-25 comparatives are derived as FY25 less H1-25 and are flagged as such.

**Third upgrade of the year: FY26 adj. EBITDA now '>€300m' (~$336m).** The path: FY25 results (26 Mar) left consensus at €205–225m; 9 Jul update set '≥€270m'; 10 Sep H1 results held '>€270m'; 10 Nov lifts to '>€300m' — 7.5% above the €279m mean (range €271–285m, 7 analysts) and the top end of the €250–300m medium-term range set in early 2025, reached ~two years early.

**The upgrade is almost entirely the Americas, specifically Hard Rock Digital's PMR product in Florida.** The RNS cites PMR revenues that 'continued to perform strongly in H2' (vs the H1 guidance of normalisation to a 'more sustainable level'), plus Mexico and Colombia post-World Cup tailwinds. Implied H2-26 adj. EBITDA is >€137.5m (~$154m): −15% HoH but +30% YoY vs derived H2-25 €105.4m, and ~€30m above the >€107.5m implied by the prior ≥€270m guide.

**But the same RNS pre-warns on 2027 and declines to guide.** Three named headwinds: (1) third-party PMR suppliers in Florida are 'now expected to have a more material impact on Playtech's wallet share into 2027'; (2) Brazil — a three-month 2026 EBITDA hit from MP 1.394 is absorbed within >€300m, but 'a more significant impact' in 2027 if the shutdown holds; (3) UK Remote Gaming Duty 21%→40% (Apr-26) annualises, with 'increased taxation across other European markets'. Management points to FY27 consensus of €266m (~$298m), −11% vs the FY26 floor — an unusually explicit way of endorsing a down year.

**H1-26 was a step change, not a beat on a soft base.** Revenue €425.1m (~$477m), +10% YoY (+13% HoH); adj. EBITDA €162.5m (~$182m), +77% YoY and +54% HoH; group adj. EBITDA margin 38.2% (+1,450bps YoY, +1,020bps HoH). Reported EBITDA €86.8m (~$97.3m) vs €12.9m; reported PAT €98.1m (~$110m) vs a €78.1m loss, helped by €80.7m of unrealised fair-value gains (HRD stake, Wplay option).

**B2B is the engine: revenue +14% (17% underlying) to €394.8m (~$443m), adj. EBITDA +75% to €128.1m (~$144m), margin 32.4% (+1,340bps).** The margin bridge is 14% revenue growth against a 3% cost reduction (B2B costs €266.7m): R&D −5%, G&A −6%, S&M flat at 2.6% of revenue, operations −1%. Pure operating leverage on a high-margin incremental revenue stream (Florida PMR) rather than a structural cost programme.

**US & Canada revenue +161% (+176% cc) to €56.9m (~$63.8m); US by licensee location +232% to €50.1m.** Six regulated iGaming states after Connecticut; multi-state launches with Fanatics (NJ/MI/PA/WV), FanDuel (WV/CT casino & Live, iPoker in MI/NJ/PA), DraftKings (CT Live), Bet365 (MI Live), Ember Casino (ex-Delaware North) on PAM+ in NJ. HRD live in NJ, MI and FL; PMR is Florida-only 'for the time being'.

**Latin America +14% reported / +29% underlying to €99.9m (~$112m); Colombia revenue >+100%.** Colombia benefited from the 19% deposit VAT being suspended (1 Jan) and replaced by a 16% GGR consumption tax (Mar-26) — but the outgoing Petro administration filed a bill in July to reinstate the 19% VAT from 2027. Mexico B2B revenue €70.3m (+6%); Caliente remains the largest customer at 14.1% of group revenue.

**Europe ex-UK +2% (+10% ex-prior-year hardware) to €104.5m; UK −8% (−5% cc) to €59.0m; RoW +23% to €8.1m.** UK decline reflects RGD plus one operator insourcing SSBTs and contractual changes with another. Regulated revenue is 83% of B2B (81%); unregulated €66.4m (+2%) — Alberta moved to regulated from 13 Jul 2026.

**SaaS and Live are the structural positives.** SaaS +20% to €69.0m (~$77.4m), now 17% of B2B across ~2,000 brands/~80 licensees (Brazil, Greece, Mexico, Spain, UK). Live revenue +8% (+12% regulated) with adj. EBITDA margin +550bps to 26.6% after table optimisation (c.500→c.480 tables); 'EGR Live Casino Supplier of the Year 2026'; AI 'Virtual Host' launched July.

**Investment income €34.2m (~$38.4m), +73%, is 21% of group adj. EBITDA.** Caliente Interactive (30.8%) share of income €30.1m (~$33.8m) vs €20.3m for three months in H1-25 — i.e. run-rate roughly flat, with June World Cup marketing a drag and Q2-25 having had exceptional sports results. HRD dividends €4.4m (~$4.9m), +110%; HRD fair value marked to €246.7m (~$277m) from €178.8m, >3x the ~€80m 2023 cost.

**Cash conversion was the headline quality signal: FCF €101.0m (~$113m) vs €6.6m, already above the €70–100m medium-term range in a single half.** Driven by EBITDA plus a €35.6m net Caliente dividend (H2-25: €31.3m). Capex + capitalised development €42.1m; adj. cash tax rate 15.1% (Caliente dividend is tax-exempt). Statutory operating cash flow was a lower €55.1m after €27.2m Snaitech CGT and €36.3m incentive-plan payments.

**Balance sheet: net cash €39.2m (~$44.0m) vs €28.5m at Dec-25; adj. gross cash €338.1m (~$379m) against the €300m 5.875% 2028 bond; €225m RCF undrawn.** Net cash/LTM adj. EBITDA ≈ −0.15x. The investment portfolio (Caliente €706.3m, HRD €246.7m, Wplay option €89.8m, LSports €56.5m) is carried at €1,134.1m (~$1.27bn) — larger than the ~£1.05bn market cap.

**Capital return: 10% of share capital bought back for ~€100m since Sep-25 (€24.6m/1.8% in H1-26; €77m/8.3% in H2-25), all into the EBT.** CFO on the call: intention is to 'return what we see as structural surplus capital'; the board 'regularly discusses' dividends and buybacks; no immediate M&A. No new programme was announced with the Nov update — a notable omission given the cash build.

**No formal cost-transformation programme; efficiencies are organic.** Restructuring costs fell to €1.6m (H1-25: €5.0m); R&D −5% from 'cost optimisation and business restructuring'; Live table rationalisation; AI deployment. Adjusting items remain heavy: €15.9m share-based pay, €13.4m incentive arrangements, €7.0m professional fees, €19.3m NorthStar/loan provisions — a €75.7m gap between reported and adjusted EBITDA.

**Governance/legal watch items.** (i) NorthStar (Ontario): full €28.9m (CAD 46.9m) ECL provision on Playtech's loan guarantee after an OSC cease-trade order and auditor resignation. (ii) Evolution/Black Cube: NJ judge denied (without prejudice, 5 Jun 26) Evolution's motion to add Playtech plc; UPEPA hearing scheduled Nov-26; no claim served. (iii) Sun Bingo under strategic review since FY25 results; RGD at 40% 'materially' deteriorates its long-term profitability.

**Brazil is the binary.** MP 1.394 (25 Sep 26) banned fixed-odds betting and online casino; sites offline from 6 Oct; licences extinguished 25 Oct; the congressional deadline of 23 Nov was extended 60 days (Act 118, 11 Nov). Playtech's 'major strategic partnership' expected to sign late-2026 is now, per the H1 call, targeted to conclude and launch 'around the beginning of next year'; H1 Brazil investment and a São Paulo Live studio are sunk.

**Medium-term targets to be reset after year-end.** Management said on the H1 call the Brazil opportunity and PMR 'did not exist when we agreed the targets' and the €250–300m / €70–100m ranges will be revisited post-FY26. Expect new targets alongside FY26 results in March 2027 — the key re-rating catalyst, or the moment the 2027 air-pocket is quantified.

**Thesis read-through: 2026 is a peak-quality, peak-cyclicality year.** The bull case (B2B pure-play, 83% regulated, net cash, €1.1bn investment book, 10% share count shrink) is intact; the bear case (one product/one customer/one state drove the upgrade, Caliente = 14% of revenue and ~€66m of cash income, Brazil/UK/Colombia tax risk) is now explicitly validated by management's own FY27 framing. The shares' reversal on upgrade day says the market is already looking through 2026.

segments.name: B2B (platform, content, Live, SaaS, services)
segments.headline: H1 B2B adj. EBITDA +75% to €128.1m on a 32% margin as Americas revenue rose ~60% underlying; the Nov update says Florida PMR stayed strong through October, but that is the revenue line now being competed away into 2027.
narrative: They delivered B2B revenue of €394.8m (~$443m) in H1 2026, +14% reported and +17% on an underlying basis once the €10.0m of legacy Caliente 'additional services fee' in Q1-25 is stripped out, and +16% half-on-half against a derived H2-25 of €340.7m. Regulated revenue grew 16% (21% underlying) to €328.4m (~$368m), lifting the regulated mix to 83% from 81%, while unregulated revenue was essentially flat at €66.4m (+2%) ahead of Alberta's reclassification to regulated from 13 July. Adj. EBITDA rose 75% to €128.1m (~$144m) and the margin expanded 1,340bps to 32.4% (H2-25 derived: 20.0%). The margin arithmetic is simple and worth being honest about: revenue +€47m, costs −€7.6m. B2B costs fell 3% to €266.7m with R&D −5% to €58.6m (cost optimisation and restructuring; capitalised development steady at 27% of R&D), G&A −6% to €45.0m (lapping non-recurring legal/advisory in 2025), sales & marketing flat at €10.4m or 2.6% of revenue, and operations −1% to €152.7m as 2025's hardware-heavy customer launch rolled off and was partly replaced by Americas investment. There is no named cost programme; this is operating leverage on an unusually high-margin incremental revenue stream rather than a structurally reset cost base, and the H2 implied margin will tell us how much of it sticks.

The US and Canada remained the growth engine, with revenue +161% (+176% constant currency) to €56.9m (~$63.8m), and +117% half-on-half from a derived €26.2m. On the licensee-location cut in Note 9, US revenue alone rose from €15.1m to €50.1m (+232%). The disclosed driver is unambiguous: the Games powered by Past Motor Racing (PMR) sports-betting product supplied to Hard Rock Bet/Seminole in Florida, where Playtech was first to market after more than a year of investment. On the H1 call they were explicit that HRD's contribution would 'trend toward a lower but more sustainable level' in H2 as Hard Rock introduces other third-party PMR suppliers; the November RNS then said PMR revenues 'continued to perform strongly in H2' but that the third-party impact on wallet share is 'now expected to be more material into 2027'. Read together, normalisation was slower than guided in H2-26 (hence the upgrade) and will be sharper in 2027 (hence the warning). PMR is Florida-only 'for the time being'; management hinted at the retail precedent for historical-racing products in other states but gave nothing bankable. Beyond PMR, the footprint widened to six regulated iGaming states via Connecticut, with multi-state launches for Fanatics (casino in NJ, MI, PA, WV), FanDuel (casino and Live into WV/CT, iPoker in MI/NJ/PA), DraftKings (Live in CT), Bet365 (Live in MI) and Ember Casino, the rebranded Delaware North, on PAM+ in New Jersey, with Ocean and Parx progressing. HRD itself is live in New Jersey, Michigan and Florida. Canada added Ontario launches including Superbet and growth from DraftKings and FanDuel, with Alberta's mid-July regulation the next step. Market-share or GGR-share data for Playtech content in US iGaming is not disclosed.

Latin America revenue was €99.9m (~$112m), +14% reported, +7% in constant currency and +29% underlying, and +35% half-on-half. Mexico B2B revenue by licensee location rose 6% to €70.3m; the Caliente relationship is now a 30.8% equity-accounted stake plus a software licence that grew 'strongly' on both sports and iGaming, with $140m of fixed fees being recognised straight-line over eight years (€7.5m in H1; €26.0m still deferred). Caliente is still the single largest customer at 14.1% of group revenue (15.1%). Colombia revenue more than doubled on the Wplay structured agreement, helped by the Constitutional Court suspending the 19% deposit VAT on 1 January and the government substituting a 16% GGR consumption tax in March — a far more sustainable base. The caveat is explicit in the release: the outgoing Petro administration submitted a bill in July to permanently reinstate the 19% deposit VAT from 2027, and the new administration's own tax reform is due in H2-26. Colombia is thus a 2027 swing factor in both directions. Brazil contributed via GaleraBet and SaaS content, with a São Paulo Live studio completed and a 'major strategic partnership' that was to sign in late 2026 — on the call, management conceded election-year concerns and now targets concluding and launching 'around the beginning of next year'. Since then MP 1.394 has taken the regulated market offline (6 October) and extinguished licences (25 October); Playtech will absorb three months of lost EBITDA within the >€300m guide, but a 2027 hit is unquantified and depends on Congress, whose review window was just extended 60 days.

Europe ex-UK grew 2% to €104.5m (~$117m), or 10% excluding non-recurring hardware sales in H1-25, essentially flat half-on-half against €105.4m. Spain (Codere, Cirsa, Bet365, Entain brands) and Poland (Totalizator across platform, casino and Live) were the call-outs. The UK fell 8% (−5% constant currency) to €59.0m (~$66.2m), −8% half-on-half, on the initial impact of Remote Gaming Duty moving from 21% to 40% in April 2026, one operator insourcing self-service betting terminals and contractual changes with another. The RNS flags that UK RGD will have 'a full year of impact' in 2027 alongside rising taxes elsewhere in Europe; the November 2025 Budget also set a 25% remote betting duty from April 2027, which will squeeze UK operator marketing and supplier revenue-share pools further. Rest of World rose 23% to €8.1m on South Africa (Hollywoodbets, Betway, Tsogo Sun) and the December 2025 LottoStar launch. By licensee location, Rest of Europe was €141.4m (+2%) and the UK €60.3m (−7%).

Product-wise, the mix is shifting toward recurring, lower-touch revenue. SaaS grew 20% to €69.0m (~$77.4m), now 17% of B2B, serving ~2,000 brands across ~80 licensees with Brazil, Greece, Mexico, Spain and the UK the strongest demand pockets — notable because it reaches operators outside the PAM+ platform and dilutes customer concentration. Live revenue grew 8% (12% in regulated markets) while a deliberate reduction in tables to c.480 from c.500 and cost measures lifted Live adj. EBITDA margin 550bps to 26.6%; the AI 'Virtual Host' launched in July with several customers and the Chroma-based studio tooling shortens branded-table lead times. Licensee (revenue-share) fees rose 18% to €248.0m, fixed-fee income 27% to €36.1m, cost-based revenue 7% to €35.7m, and the legacy Caliente services fee halved to €5.1m. Playtech Protect reached 41 brands across 16 jurisdictions (from 28). Standard operator KPIs — handle, net/structural sports margin, promo intensity, actives, ARPU — are not applicable or disclosed for a B2B supplier; the equivalent quality metrics here are regulated mix (83%), SaaS share (17%), S&M intensity (2.6%) and customer concentration (14.1%).

For the segment outlook, management said H2 adj. EBITDA would be lower than H1 on HRD normalisation, Brazil investment ahead of signing and a full half of UK RGD; the November update implies group H2 of >€137.5m, which on a flat investment-income assumption of ~€34m would put H2 B2B+B2C operating EBITDA somewhere around €100–105m [our estimate], i.e. a B2B margin in the mid-to-high 20s rather than 32%. That is still well above the 20–21% of 2025 and is the right base to underwrite into 2027, before subtracting PMR share loss, Brazil and UK duty. We would treat anything above a 25% B2B margin in FY27 as requiring either a Brazil re-opening or evidence that PMR can travel beyond Florida.

segments.name: Investments (Caliente Interactive 30.8%, Hard Rock Digital, Wplay option, other)
segments.headline: Investment income €34.2m (21% of group adj. EBITDA) plus €35.6m of Caliente cash dividends; HRD marked up 38% to €246.7m. The book is worth more than the market cap but is concentrated in two Americas counterparties.
narrative: They reported adjusted investment income of €34.2m (~$38.4m), +73% YoY but −19% against a derived H2-25 of €42.0m, which is now 21% of group adj. EBITDA and the piece of the P&L that most distinguishes Playtech from a conventional supplier. The bulk is the 30.8% equity-accounted stake in Caliente Interactive (formerly Caliplay), which contributed €30.1m (~$33.8m) versus €20.3m in H1-25 — but H1-25 was only a three-month contribution (the revised agreement became effective 31 March 2025), so the like-for-like run-rate was roughly flat-to-down, with June's World Cup marketing push a drag and Q2-25 having enjoyed exceptional sporting results. Management expects higher volumes in H2 as World Cup acquisition converts, and the November RNS confirmed Mexico 'benefitted from tailwinds' post-tournament. Other associates netted to a €2.4m loss (LSports −€1.5m, NorthStar −€0.7m, Sporting News −€0.3m, Algosport +€0.1m), leaving share of income from associates at €27.7m (~$31.1m).

Cash is the more important signal here. Caliente paid gross dividends of €37.4m (€35.6m net of withholding) in H1-26 after €31.3m in H2-25 and nil in H1-25; these are excluded from adj. EBITDA (which carries the equity-accounted share of income instead) but are added back in the FCF definition, which is why FCF of €101.0m exceeds operating EBITDA. The carrying value of Caliente is €706.3m (~$792m), essentially flat on December. The $140m fixed-fee element of the 2025 restructuring is being recognised straight-line over eight years in B2B fixed-fee income (€7.5m in H1). Caliente's position as co-host-market leader through the World Cup gives it visibility, but it remains ~14% of consolidated revenue and roughly €66m of annualised cash income on top — the concentration the bear case rests on.

Hard Rock Digital paid dividends of €4.4m (~$4.9m), +110% YoY but below the derived €8.2m in H2-25 (FY25: €10.3m); these are inside adj. EBITDA. The minority equity stake was marked up to €246.7m (~$277m) from €178.8m at December — more than three times the ~€80m invested in 2023 — and drove the bulk of a €69.0m unrealised fair-value gain in reported profit. The Wplay (Colombia) call option rose to €89.8m (~$101m) from €75.6m on improved Colombian tax arrangements, and a listed stake was partly sold for a €2.1m realised gain. Total investment-book carrying value is €1,134.1m (~$1.27bn) versus a market capitalisation of roughly £1.05bn at 364.8p — the sum-of-the-parts argument is obvious, but the two largest line items are illiquid private stakes whose value is tethered to Florida sports betting and Mexican online gaming respectively.

The negative item is NorthStar Gaming (Ontario): following an OSC cease-trade order, auditor resignation and continued losses, Playtech took a full €28.9m (CAD 46.9m) expected-credit-loss provision against its guarantee of NorthStar's loan facility (up from €12.2m at December), excluded from adj. EBITDA. It is a small number against the book but a reminder that the 'structured agreement' model carries credit and governance tail risk, and that disclosure around the other options (Wplay, Brazil's GaleraBet, the pending Brazilian partner) deserves scrutiny as the Brazilian ban plays out.

blocks.takeaway: Adjusted investment income of €34.2m is 21% of group adj. EBITDA, mostly the 30.8% Caliente stake contributing €30.1m.
points: Investment income €34.2m (~$38.4m), +73% YoY but −19% against derived H2-25 €42.0m; the P&L piece most distinguishing Playtech from a conventional supplier.
Caliente contributed €30.1m (~$33.8m) versus €20.3m in H1-25, which was only three months (agreement effective 31 March 2025); like-for-like roughly flat-to-down.
June's World Cup marketing push was a drag; Q2-25 enjoyed exceptional sporting results. Management expects higher H2 volumes; November RNS said Mexico 'benefitted from tailwinds'.
Other associates netted a €2.4m loss (LSports −€1.5m, NorthStar −€0.7m, Sporting News −€0.3m, Algosport +€0.1m); share of associates income €27.7m (~$31.1m).

blocks.heading: Caliente cash and concentration
blocks.takeaway: Caliente paid €35.6m net dividends in H1-26, lifting FCF to €101.0m above operating EBITDA, but concentration is the bear case.
points: Gross dividends €37.4m (€35.6m net of withholding) after €31.3m in H2-25 and nil in H1-25; excluded from adj. EBITDA but added back in FCF.
Carrying value €706.3m (~$792m), essentially flat on December; $140m fixed fee recognised straight-line over eight years in B2B (€7.5m in H1).
Caliente is co-host-market leader through the World Cup, but remains ~14% of consolidated revenue plus roughly €66m annualised cash income.

blocks.heading: Hard Rock Digital and book value
blocks.takeaway: HRD marked up 38% to €246.7m; total investment book €1,134.1m exceeds the ~£1.05bn market cap but rests on two illiquid stakes.
points: HRD dividends €4.4m (~$4.9m), +110% YoY but below derived €8.2m in H2-25 (FY25: €10.3m); inside adj. EBITDA.
HRD stake marked to €246.7m (~$277m) from €178.8m, over three times the ~€80m invested in 2023, driving most of a €69.0m unrealised fair-value gain.
Wplay (Colombia) call option rose to €89.8m (~$101m) from €75.6m on improved tax arrangements; listed stake partly sold for €2.1m realised gain.
Total book €1,134.1m (~$1.27bn) versus market cap roughly £1.05bn at 364.8p; two largest items tethered to Florida sports betting and Mexican online gaming.

blocks.heading: NorthStar risk
blocks.takeaway: A full €28.9m provision against NorthStar's loan guarantee shows the structured-agreement model carries credit and governance tail risk.
points: Following an OSC cease-trade order, auditor resignation and continued losses, Playtech took a full €28.9m (CAD 46.9m) expected-credit-loss provision, up from €12.2m at December.
Excluded from adj. EBITDA; small against the book but a reminder of tail risk.
Disclosure around other options (Wplay, Brazil's GaleraBet, the pending Brazilian partner) deserves scrutiny as the Brazilian ban plays out.

segments.name: B2C (Sun Bingo & Other, HAPPYBET wind-down)
segments.headline: Revenue −22% to €32.0m and adj. EBITDA a token €0.2m; HAPPYBET is nearly gone and Sun Bingo's economics are structurally impaired by 40% RGD. A strategic review is live and the segment is 'lower strategic focus'.
narrative: They reported B2C revenue of €32.0m (~$35.9m), −22% YoY and −15% half-on-half, with adj. EBITDA of €0.2m versus a €1.5m loss in H1-25 and a derived €4.7m loss in H2-25. The segment is now 7.5% of group revenue and effectively nil of EBITDA; management describes it as 'an area of lower strategic focus'. Sun Bingo and Other B2C — the UK bingo brand operated under a long-term agreement with News UK — generated €31.7m (~$35.5m), −5% YoY, with a €4.5m decline in Sun Bingo itself partly offset by €3.0m growth in 'Other'. Costs fell 7% to €30.2m as marketing, processing fees and News UK's profit share all dropped, and the €2.0m half-yearly minimum-guarantee release that burdened 2025 fell away after that prepayment was fully impaired at December. The net result was adj. EBITDA of €1.5m (H1-25: €0.8m) — a better number on a worse business.

The structural problem is UK tax. Remote Gaming Duty rose from 21% to 40% in April 2026, which the company says results in 'a material deterioration of the long-term profitability outlook for Sun Bingo', compounding the stricter affordability and marketing rules in place since H2-24 that have cut active players and player value. H1-26 carries only one quarter of the higher rate; H2 carries two, and management lists this as one of the three reasons H2 group EBITDA will be below H1. A strategic review of Sun Bingo was launched with the FY25 results; no conclusion was given in September or November. With a near-zero EBITDA contribution, any exit is immaterial to earnings but would simplify the story and remove a UK-regulatory exposure that otherwise forces management to discuss operator economics they no longer want to own.

HAPPYBET (Germany) is essentially done: revenue −96% to €0.3m and the adj. EBITDA loss narrowed 43% to €1.3m (H1-25: −€2.3m; derived H2-25: −€4.0m), with the wind-down expected to complete by end-2026. The remaining cost base of €1.6m should fall to zero in 2027, a small but real tailwind of ~€2–3m annualised against the 2027 headwinds. Operator-style KPIs (actives, ARPU, handle, margin) are not disclosed for B2C.

Our read is that B2C is now a disposal candidate rather than a segment, and the right way to model it is adj. EBITDA of roughly zero in H2-26 and FY27 with downside if the Sun Bingo contract is retained at 40% RGD. The only reason it matters to the equity story is optionality on a clean exit and the signal it sends on capital discipline.

highlights.text: FY26 adj. EBITDA guide raised to >€300m (~$336m) — the third upgrade of 2026, 7.5% above the €279m consensus and +52% on FY25 — with H1 already at €162.5m (+77%) and management citing continued H2 strength in Florida PMR and post-World Cup Mexico/Colombia.

B2B operating leverage: revenue +14% (17% underlying) with costs −3% drove the B2B margin to 32.4% (+1,340bps YoY, +1,240bps HoH); Live margin +550bps to 26.6% on table optimisation; S&M only 2.6% of revenue.

Cash conversion: FCF €101.0m (~$113m) in one half vs the €70–100m annual medium-term target, net cash €39.2m after a €24.6m buyback and €63.5m of Snaitech CGT/incentive payments; 10% of share capital retired for ~€100m since Sep-25.
Regulated mix rising (83% of B2B; 84% of group) with SaaS +20% to €69.0m (17% of B2B, ~2,000 brands) — the recurring, lower-concentration revenue the multiple should ultimately be built on.
US footprint broadened beyond HRD: six iGaming states, multi-state launches with Fanatics, FanDuel, DraftKings, Bet365 and Ember Casino on PAM+; US licensee-location revenue +232% to €50.1m.
Investment book marked at €1,134m (~$1.27bn), above the ~£1.05bn market cap: HRD stake €246.7m (>3x cost), Caliente €706.3m paying €35.6m net cash dividends in H1 and ~€66m annualised.
Colombia revenue >+100% after the 19% deposit VAT was replaced by a 16% GGR consumption tax; Wplay option marked up to €89.8m.

lowlights.text: The upgrade is one product, one customer, one state: Florida PMR with Hard Rock. Management now says third-party PMR suppliers will have a 'more material impact on wallet share into 2027' — the RNS reads as a peak-year marker, and FY27 consensus (€266m) sits 11% below the FY26 floor.

Brazil shutdown (MP 1.394): regulated sites offline since 6 Oct, licences extinguished 25 Oct, congressional review extended 60 days. A three-month 2026 hit is absorbed; 2027 impact is 'more significant' and unquantified, and the long-trailed 'major strategic partnership' has slipped to early-2027 at best after a year of sunk investment.

UK: RGD 21%→40% from Apr-26 annualises in 2027, remote betting duty rises to 25% from Apr-27; UK B2B revenue already −8% and Sun Bingo's long-term profitability 'materially' impaired, strategic review unresolved.

Concentration: Caliente is 14.1% of group revenue plus €30.1m of equity income and €35.6m of cash dividends; Caliente plus HRD likely account for well over a third of group adj. EBITDA [our estimate — HRD B2B revenue not disclosed].

Adjusting items remain heavy: €75.7m gap between reported (€86.8m) and adjusted (€162.5m) EBITDA, including €15.9m share-based pay, €13.4m incentive arrangements, €7.0m professional fees and a €28.9m full provision on the NorthStar loan guarantee after an OSC cease-trade order.

No new capital-return programme accompanied the November upgrade despite the cash build; the Evolution/Black Cube litigation (UPEPA hearing Nov-26) and Colombia's proposed VAT reinstatement from 2027 are open tails.
Shares reversed from +4.5% intraday to −1.0% at the close on upgrade day and are ~18% below the mid-September high — the market is pricing 2027, not 2026.

forecast.intro: Guidance has moved three times in 2026: from a post-FY25 consensus of €219m (range €205–225m) to '≥€270m' on 9 July (H1 >€155m), held at '>€270m' with H1 results on 10 September, and to '>€300m' on 10 November against a €279m consensus (€271–285m). Every step was driven by the B2B Americas line — specifically Hard Rock Digital's PMR product in Florida normalising more slowly than guided — with Mexico and Colombia post-World Cup volumes as the secondary contributor. Brazil's three-month shutdown is absorbed inside the new floor. The November RNS pointedly gives no FY27 guidance but cites FY27 consensus of €266m and lists three headwinds (PMR competition, Brazil, UK RGD annualisation), which we read as management steering the Street toward a double-digit EBITDA decline next year.

bridge.title: Florida PMR / HRD slower normalisation + US iGaming state expansion
Mexico & Colombia post-World Cup volumes, less Brazil 3-month shutdown
bridge.change: LatAm B2B + Caliente share of income

forecast.view: **H2-26 / FY26.** We model FY26 adj. EBITDA of c.€303–308m (~$340–345m) [estimate], i.e. H2 of c.€140–145m: operating EBITDA c.€105–110m (B2B margin high-20s on H2 B2B revenue of c.€380–400m, down from 32% as HRD normalises and UK duty bites) plus investment income c.€35m. FY26 revenue c.€820–840m (~$920–940m) [estimate; not guided]. FCF should land c.€150–170m for the year given H1 €101m and a second Caliente dividend, taking year-end net cash to c.€100–130m before any further buyback — ample room for a renewed programme alongside FY26 results. **FY27.** The honest base case is a decline: FY27 consensus €266m implies −11% vs the FY26 floor, and we think the risk is skewed slightly below that if Brazil stays shut all year (Playtech's Brazil B2B revenue is not disclosed, but the lost GaleraBet/SaaS/Live contribution plus the delayed partnership is a multi-year growth hole) and PMR wallet share halves. Offsets: full-year Connecticut/Alberta, SaaS compounding at ~20%, HAPPYBET costs to zero, Colombia if VAT is not reinstated, and continued Caliente growth. **Margin direction:** B2B margin should settle in the mid-20s in FY27 versus ~29–30% for FY26 [estimates]; group adj. margin high-20s to ~30%. **Leverage:** net cash rising; with the €300m 5.875% bond due June 2028, expect refinancing discussion at a smaller quantum and a formal capital-allocation framework with the March results. The medium-term targets (€250–300m / €70–100m) will be re-based then; a credible new range would need to start from the FY27 trough, not the FY26 peak.
watch: Brazil: whether Congress converts, amends or lets MP 1.394 lapse within the extended 60-day window; any Supreme Court ruling; timing/terms of the 'major strategic partnership' and whether it is still live.
Florida PMR: the pace at which Hard Rock onboards competing PMR suppliers and Playtech's residual wallet share; any evidence PMR can be licensed in other states or to other operators.
FY26 results (c. March 2027): H2 B2B margin, Brazil revenue disclosure, re-based medium-term targets, and a new buyback/dividend framework given net cash >€100m [est.].
UK: full-year 40% RGD impact on UK B2B (−8% in H1) and the Sun Bingo strategic-review outcome; 25% remote betting duty from April 2027.
Colombia tax: fate of the Petro bill to reinstate 19% deposit VAT from 2027 versus the 16% GGR consumption tax; Wplay option value.
Caliente Interactive: H2 post-World Cup volume conversion, dividend cadence (€35.6m H1), and customer concentration at 14% of revenue.
Evolution/Black Cube litigation (UPEPA hearing Nov-26) and NorthStar recovery; the €300m 2028 bond refinancing plan.
